Campbell County property tax guide FAQ

Who handles assessment appeals in Campbell County?

Campbell County by the numbers

Where is Campbell County, Wyoming, and what is in it?

Campbell County sits in northeast Wyoming, with Gillette as both the county seat and the largest city. Wikipedia lists the county at about 4,800 square miles, and it was created on February 21, 1911, from land taken from Crook and Weston Counties.

The neighbors are Powder River County, Montana, to the north, Crook and Weston Counties to the east, Converse County to the south, and Johnson and Sheridan Counties to the west. The county forms the Gillette micropolitan area. Gillette itself was founded in 1891 as a Burlington railroad town and was incorporated on January 6, 1892, according to its Wikipedia entry.

That is a very large county with very few people per square mile. For a seller, the practical result is that parcels range from small city lots in Gillette to rural acreage, and the same assessor and treasurer handle all of them.

What are the key numbers for Campbell County?

The Census Bureau puts the Campbell County population at 48,145 as of July 1, 2025. The table below collects the figures we confirmed from the Census QuickFacts page and the county offices.

ItemFigure
Population estimate, July 1, 202548,145
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202477.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$279,100
Households, 2020 to 202417,988
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$89,869
Land area4,802.07 square miles
Residential assessment level9.5% of market value
Gillette elevation4,554 feet

With nearly 78 percent of households owning their home, most Campbell County property tax bills land on families, not landlords.

How does coal shape the Campbell County tax base?

Coal makes up a large share of what Campbell County taxes. A WyoFile report from November 2021 said the county and Gillette supply about 40 percent of the nation's coal for electricity, and that coal was about 51.6 percent of the county's assessed value in 2021, down from 58.6 percent in 2017.

The same report said assessed valuation fell by $850 million from 2020 to 2021, the lowest level since 2004. Those are 2021 figures, so check the current numbers with the assessor.

Why does this matter to a homeowner? Wyoming taxes minerals and industrial property very differently from houses. The Wyoming Taxpayers Association guide lists minerals at 100 percent of fair market value, industrial property at 11.5 percent, and all other real and personal property at 9.5 percent. When the mine and industrial base changes, the mill levy spread across homes can change with it.

How is a Campbell County house assessed and taxed?

A Campbell County house is valued as of January 1, multiplied by 9.5 percent, then multiplied by the total mill levy for its location. The University of Wyoming Extension says residential levies run from 65 to 80 mills depending on location, with one mill equal to $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Here is how the math works on a hypothetical $279,100 house, the county median from the Census table above, at an illustrative 70 mills:

  • Assessed value: $279,100 x 9.5% = about $26,515
  • Tax before exemptions: $26,515 x 0.070 = about $1,856

That is an example, not your bill. Your actual mills depend on the city, school and special districts that cover your parcel.

The assessor and the treasurer do different jobs. The Assessor's Office values property and says it does not set tax amounts or collect taxes. The Treasurer bills and collects.

What exemptions and refunds can reduce a Campbell County bill?

Wyoming's 2025 law, Senate File 69, gives owner-occupied homes an exemption of 25 percent of the first $1 million of value. The legislative summary says it applies from tax year 2025 and, starting in tax year 2026, requires the owner to live in the home at least eight months a year.

A February 2026 Wyoming Public Media story reported that owners had to file an affidavit with the county assessor by March 1 that year. Ask the Campbell County assessor what the filing rule is for the next tax year.

  • The exemption covers an owner-occupied single-family house, condo, townhouse or manufactured home.
  • Someone who receives the long-term homeowner exemption on the same property cannot also take it for the same year.
  • The Campbell County Treasurer's page links to a Property Tax Refund Program.

A rental or a vacant inherited house does not meet the eight-month residence test, so check with the assessor before assuming the exemption applies.

How do you appeal a Campbell County assessment?

You start by filing a written statement with the county assessor within 30 days after the assessment schedule was sent. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 sets that window, and the statement has to say why the assessment is wrong.

The Campbell County Assessor's page links to an Appeals Process page and an Important Dates page, so use those for this year's calendar. In Laramie County, for comparison, the county page says schedules are mailed on or before the fourth Monday of April and that owners can ask for an informal review before a formal appeal.

Gather what a board would want to see:

  • Your notice of value and parcel number
  • Recent sales of similar Gillette or rural houses, if you have them
  • Photos and repair estimates for condition problems the assessor may not have seen
  • An appraisal, if you ordered one

Residential sales data is confidential in Wyoming, so the office may not email or phone it to you.

What does Gillette's climate mean for a house?

Gillette gets about 17.59 inches of precipitation a year and about 55.7 inches of snow, according to the city's Wikipedia climate summary. May is the wettest month at 3.27 inches, and December through February each average 8 to 9 inches of snow.

Buyers and appraisers notice roofs, furnaces and foundations first in a climate like that. A house with an old roof or a failing heating system may be assessed on the same basis as its neighbors even though it needs money spent on it. If that describes your property, say so in writing when you ask for a review.

How does a Campbell County tax sale work?

In Campbell County the treasurer does not sell your house. The county sells its tax lien to a bidder, and the county's tax sale page describes the sale as buyer beware.

  • Notice of the sale and the list of properties is published three consecutive weeks in a legal newspaper in the county.
  • The buyer pays the unpaid taxes, interest and costs, and receives a certificate of purchase the day of the sale.
  • An owner can redeem by paying the tax sold, a 3% penalty, 15% simple interest, a redemption fee and any later taxes the holder paid.
  • Applying for a tax deed requires the holder to show compliance with Wyoming Statute 39-13-108, and the page says no deed can issue after six years from the original sale.

The page gives conflicting timeframes for deed applications, four years in some places and five in others, so call the treasurer before relying on a date.

What can you do about unpaid tax before selling in Campbell County?

Start by asking the Treasurer for the exact balance, then decide how you want to close. Wyoming bills are due in two halves, November 10 and May 10, and the Campbell tax sale page confirms those dates for new-year taxes, with interest starting the day after each due date.

An unpaid balance does not stop you from selling, but it has to be dealt with at closing. A cash buyer can take the house as-is, and the title company can pay the county from the sale proceeds.

Offices to call:

  • Treasurer, 500 S. Gillette Ave., Suite 1700, Gillette: 307-682-7268
  • Assessor, Suite 1300 in the same building: 307-682-7266
  • County Clerk: 307-682-7285
  • Planning and Zoning, and Building, through Public Works: 307-682-1970

The Treasurer also keeps a Wright office at 395 Lariat Way, open Wednesdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., weather permitting.

More questions about Campbell County, WY Property Tax Guide

Who bills property tax in Campbell County, Wyoming?

The Campbell County Treasurer bills and collects it. The Assessor's Office only values the property, and says on its page that it does not set or collect tax.

What percent of value is a Campbell County home taxed on?

9.5 percent of fair market value. The mill levy for your location is then applied to that assessed value, and levies for homes run from 65 to 80 mills according to University of Wyoming Extension.

How long do I have to contest my Campbell County valuation?

Thirty days from the date the assessment schedule was sent. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 sets the window, so file your written statement with the assessor early and check the county's Important Dates page.

Can I sell a Campbell County house with back taxes?

Yes, but the balance has to be paid or handled at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure, and call us at (424) 435-2326 if you want a written cash offer for the house as it stands.

What happens at a Campbell County tax sale?

The county sells a lien, not the house. A bidder pays the delinquent taxes, interest and costs and receives a certificate of purchase, and the owner can redeem by paying what the county page lists.

Does Campbell County have a homeowner exemption?

Wyoming's 25 percent exemption on the first $1 million of value applies to owner-occupied single-family homes from tax year 2025. Owners had to file an affidavit with the assessor by March 1 in 2026, so confirm the current deadline.

Sweetwater County property tax guide FAQ

Who handles assessment appeals in Sweetwater County?

Sweetwater County by the numbers

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sweetwater County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where is Sweetwater County, Wyoming, and how big is it?

Sweetwater County is in southwestern Wyoming, borders Colorado and Utah, and is the largest county in the state by area. Wikipedia gives the total as 10,491 square miles, with the Continental Divide running through it and most of the Great Divide Basin in its northeast quadrant.

Green River is the county seat and Rock Springs is the largest city. The county was created on December 17, 1867, as Carter County, and was renamed in 1869 for the Sweetwater River. South Pass City was the first seat, and the seat moved to Green River after 1873.

For a property owner, size is the point. The county has about 4 people per square mile, so a parcel can be a city lot in Rock Springs or a long way from anything, and both are handled by the same two courthouse offices in Green River.

What are the key numbers for Sweetwater County?

The Census Bureau estimates 41,267 residents in Sweetwater County as of July 1, 2025. The table pulls together the figures we confirmed from the Census QuickFacts page and city and county sources.

ItemFigure
Population estimate, July 1, 202541,267
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202474.6%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$251,400
Households, 2020 to 202417,502
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$75,034
Rock Springs population, 2020 census23,526
Green River population, 2020 census11,825
Residential assessment level9.5% of market value

Rock Springs sits at about 6,388 feet and Green River at about 6,115 feet, according to their Wikipedia pages.

What drives the Sweetwater County economy?

Trona and the soda ash made from it are the base of the Sweetwater County economy. The Wyoming Business Council's Southwest profile says the county has the largest natural trona reserves in the world and names WE Soda and Ciner as major employers.

The Green River article says soda ash mining employs over 2,000 people at five mines, and notes the 80 MW Sweetwater Solar project near the city.

Transport matters too. The same Business Council profile describes Interstate 80 as an east-west freight corridor and says Union Pacific runs mainline and spur rail to mines and plants. Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport in Rock Springs has daily service to Denver, and Western Wyoming College is in Rock Springs.

Steady industrial payrolls tend to support the local housing market, but they also mean a large share of the tax base sits in plants and mines, not houses.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sweetwater County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How is a Sweetwater County house assessed and taxed?

The Sweetwater County Assessor values every taxable parcel as of January 1, and a house is taxed on 9.5 percent of that value. The Assessor's page says valuations follow Wyoming statutes and Department of Revenue guidelines, and that voters, commissioners, state limits and assessed values set the tax rates.

The tax is the assessed value multiplied by the mills. University of Wyoming Extension gives a range of 65 to 80 mills for residential property and a sample of a $100,000 home at 70 mills producing about $665.

  • Industrial property, including mineral processing, is assessed at 11.5 percent.
  • Minerals and mine products are assessed at 100 percent.
  • Other real and personal property, including homes, is assessed at 9.5 percent.

Those percentages come from the Wyoming Taxpayers Association. The Assessor does not bill or collect. The Treasurer does.

What exemptions and refunds apply in Sweetwater County?

Sweetwater County homeowners can have several reductions at once, and they appear at the bottom of the notice of value. The Green River Star reported in April 2025 that the 25 percent cut from Senate File 69 was applied automatically that year.

  • The veteran's exemption rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025, and veterans missing it on the notice were told to contact the assessor by May 26.
  • The long-term homeowners exemption is for owners age 65 who have paid Wyoming property taxes for 25 years, live in the home eight months a year, and bring ID showing a birthdate.
  • The Property Tax Refund Program pays up to half the median residential tax or 75 percent of the 2024 bill, whichever is less, and taxes must be paid in full before applying.

Later rules changed. A February 2026 report said owners needed to file an affidavit with the county assessor by March 1 that year. Call the Assessor at 307-872-3700 for the current process.

How do you appeal a Sweetwater County valuation?

You have 30 days from the mailing date of the notice of value to contact the Assessor and make your case. SweetwaterNOW reported in 2024 that the window is 30 days from mailing, and Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 requires a written statement of why the assessment is incorrect.

Notices usually go out in the spring. The 2025 notices were due in mailboxes in the days after April 10, per the Green River Star, and the 2024 notices after April 17.

A short checklist helps:

  • Find your parcel's value and exemptions on the notice.
  • Collect recent sales of comparable Rock Springs or Green River homes.
  • Document condition problems with photos and bids.
  • Send your written statement before the 30 days end.

The same 2024 article said Sweetwater County had the lowest residential value change in Wyoming for tax year 2022 to 2023, at 8.52 percent against a statewide average of 17.91 percent.

What should a homeowner expect from the weather in Rock Springs and Green River?

The area is semi-arid and cold. Wikipedia reports average precipitation in Rock Springs of 10.45 inches a year and average snowfall of 31.3 inches, with measurable precipitation on about 61.7 days a year.

Little rain does not mean easy winters. Freezing cold at roughly 6,000 feet is hard on roofs, pipes and furnaces, and a vacant house can develop trouble fast. If you are carrying an inherited or empty property, keep the heat on and the roof checked while the tax bill sits unpaid.

When are Sweetwater County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?

Statements are mailed in September and can be paid in full by December 31 or in two halves, the first by November 10 and the second by May 10. The Treasurer's page says weekend and holiday due dates move to the next business day, and mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date.

Pay or view a statement online at itax.sweetwatercountywy.gov. Late interest, the May 11 delinquency date and the tax lien sale are covered earlier on this page.

Real property taxes are a lien on the house, so any unpaid balance will need to be settled when the property sells.

How do you sell a Sweetwater County house with taxes due?

Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer, then decide how to close. An unpaid balance can be paid from the sale proceeds at the title company, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is without repairs.

Offices to contact, all in the Green River courthouse at 80 W. Flaming Gorge Way:

  • Treasurer, Suite 139: 307-872-3720 (the website footer shows 307-872-3970, so confirm), taxes@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Assessor, Suite 122: 307-872-3700, assessor@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Rock Springs Assessor line: 307-922-5200

Call us at (424) 435-2326 if you want a written cash offer for a Sweetwater County house.

More questions about Sweetwater County, WY Property Tax Guide

Who sends the property tax bill in Sweetwater County, Wyoming?

The County Treasurer in Green River. The Assessor values property but does not set tax amounts or collect them.

How long do I have to question my Sweetwater County notice of value?

Thirty days from the date the notice was mailed. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 calls for a written statement, so contact the Assessor at 307-872-3700 well before the window closes.

What is the residential assessment rate in Sweetwater County?

9.5 percent of market value. Industrial property is assessed at 11.5 percent and mineral production at 100 percent.

Can I sell a Sweetwater County house if I owe property tax?

Yes. The balance has to be paid or settled at closing, and the Treasurer can give you a payoff amount.

Which Sweetwater County city is the county seat?

Green River. Rock Springs is larger, with 23,526 people at the 2020 census against 11,825 in Green River.

Is there a veteran's exemption in Sweetwater County?

Yes. It rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025. A veteran who does not see it on the notice should contact the Assessor's office.
